9yjZpBq1XBE.title: Disney's FastPass: A Complicated History
9yjZpBq1XBE.summary: A feature-length Defunctland documentary on the history of Disney's FastPass and FastPass+ expedited queue systems. It covers how the systems evolved and how they were designed, with simulation of their effects on park lines.
9yjZpBq1XBE.why: HN recommends it as an accessible, engrossing lesson in queueing theory and systems design, even for people with no interest in Disney.

quote.text: If you ever wanted a feature-length explanation of queueing theory and how ignoring it makes everything worse, well... here you go

FihU5JxmnBg.title: Debugging with the Scientific Method - Stuart Halloway
FihU5JxmnBg.summary: Stuart Halloway of Cognitect argues for debugging with the scientific method: form hypotheses, try to falsify them, and write everything down. The talk is given to the Clojure community but applies to any language.
FihU5JxmnBg.why: HN recommends it as a talk that changed how people debug, worth rewatching periodically.

quote.text: changed how I debug problems. I try to watch it once every year or two.

7CgXvIuZR40.title: TasBlock at AGDQ 2017: TASBot
7CgXvIuZR40.summary: A recording of the TASBot block at Awesome Games Done Quick 2017, where a robot plays games via tool-assisted speedruns, including Super Mario 64 and Portal on an SNES via arbitrary code execution, and ending with a Twitch Plays segment. It showcases console exploits and creative hardware hacking.
7CgXvIuZR40.why: HN commenters rate it a great GDQ watch and point to its feats, such as streaming video and Skype through controller ports, as inspiring hacks.

quote.text: TASBot which always makes a great GDQ watch

XKu_SEDAykw.title: How to: Work at Google — Example Coding/Engineering Interview
XKu_SEDAykw.summary: Two Google engineers perform a mock coding interview and then discuss best practices for candidates, including asking clarifying questions and communicating while solving.
XKu_SEDAykw.why: Cited as a realistic, well-run example of a technical interview, both for candidates preparing and interviewers calibrating.

quote.text: two of the suggestions in this excellent video from Google showing an example of a great technical interview

Y0Oa4Lp5fLE.title: 2. Behavioral Evolution
Y0Oa4Lp5fLE.summary: Stanford biologist Robert Sapolsky lectures on the evolution of behavior, including the Prisoner's Dilemma and tit-for-tat strategies in animals. It is part of his Human Behavioral Biology course.
Y0Oa4Lp5fLE.why: Recommended in game-theory and cooperation threads, with the whole lecture series endorsed.

quote.text: This entire lecture series on Human Behavioral Biology is worth watching from the beginning

-2ZTmuX3cog.title: ARCHIVE TEAM: A Distributed Preservation of Service Attack
-2ZTmuX3cog.summary: Jason Scott of Archive Team describes how a loose band of volunteers rushes to copy sites like Geocities, Friendster and Yahoo Video before their owners delete them. The talk covers the tactics they use and the argument that this data is history worth saving.
-2ZTmuX3cog.why: HN points to it whenever a company shuts down a service and wipes user content, as an entertaining case for digital preservation.

quote.text: gave a fantastically entertaining talk about how they saved Geocities, Yahoo! Video, and Friendster

HrUy1Vn2KdI.title: Couldn't Care Less. Cormac McCarthy in conversation with David Krakauer
HrUy1Vn2KdI.summary: A 2017 documentary filmed at the Santa Fe Institute in which novelist Cormac McCarthy talks with SFI's David Krakauer. They discuss isolation, mathematics, character and the nature of the unconscious.
HrUy1Vn2KdI.why: It is one of the few long, candid interviews with the famously reclusive McCarthy, and commenters share it whenever he comes up.

quote.text: This is my favourite interview with him so I will take this post as an excuse to share it.

e08kOj2kISU.title: How to Speed up a Python Program 114,000 times.
e08kOj2kISU.summary: David Schachter describes how he made a data-collection Python program run 114,000 times faster, drawing on decades of experience. The talk covers pipelining, cache effects and other optimization lessons.
e08kOj2kISU.why: A favorite tech talk on HN for showing that hardware knowledge and generalist skills beat simply adding machines.

quote.text: Humour, serious technical insight and a good reminder of why being a generalist is an advantage.

uGlzRt-FYto.title: “What is Success?” by Evan Czaplicki
uGlzRt-FYto.summary: Elm creator Evan Czaplicki's 2018 Elm Europe talk on how to define success for an open source project and language community. It argues against judging projects by GitHub activity and touches on community expectations.
uGlzRt-FYto.why: Cited in debates over Elm's direction and open source health, with some praising its points about metrics and others finding its tone toward unhappy users hard to watch.

quote.text: he raises some interesting points about how measuring projects by Github activity is strongly biased

xuCn8ux2gbs.title: history of the entire world, i guess
xuCn8ux2gbs.summary: A fast, absurdist 19-minute animated run through the history of the whole world, narrated and scored by Bill Wurtz in his distinctive style. It compresses millennia of events into jokes, songs and quick visuals.
xuCn8ux2gbs.why: HN commenters list it among favorite long-form, info-dense YouTube videos and as a representative piece of Wurtz's quirky creativity.

quote.text: history of the entire world, i guess

McLq1hEq3UY.title: Lecture 1 | Convex Optimization I (Stanford)
McLq1hEq3UY.summary: The introductory lecture of Stephen Boyd's Stanford Convex Optimization I course (EE 364A). It outlines convex sets, functions and problems, and the course's coverage of least-squares, linear and semidefinite programming, duality and interior-point methods.
McLq1hEq3UY.why: HN recommends Boyd's lectures as a fantastic, often funny follow-up to linear algebra and as a step in machine learning study paths.

quote.text: These lectures are fantastic after you've mastered the basics of linear algebra

34rdxDgpaaA.title: Well There's Your Problem | Episode 28: Goiânia Incident
34rdxDgpaaA.summary: An episode of the Well There's Your Problem podcast on the 1987 Goiania radiological accident in Brazil, based largely on the IAEA report. It goes through the event day by day.
34rdxDgpaaA.why: HN points to it as a good, detailed podcast account whenever the Goiania incident or lost radioactive sources come up.

quote.text: Goes into detail day by day about the events

TiXINuf5nbI.title: Jake Thackray 'Molly Metcalfe'
TiXINuf5nbI.summary: Jake Thackray performs the folk song Molly Metcalfe, which opens with an explanation of the traditional northern English sheep-counting system (yan, tan, tethera). It is a short, witty piece of British folk songwriting.
TiXINuf5nbI.why: HN recommends it in threads about sheep-counting systems as the famous song that explains them.

quote.text: I'll again recommend the Youtube video of Jake Thackray singing 'Molly Metcalfe'

fPKMmJpAGWc.title: Introducing Nx - José Valim | Lambda Days 2021
fPKMmJpAGWc.summary: Jose Valim introduces Nx, the project bringing numerical computing to Elixir, covering multi-dimensional tensors, automatic differentiation and JIT compilation to CPU and GPU.
fPKMmJpAGWc.why: Recommended in Elixir and machine learning threads as the introduction to what Nx makes possible.

quote.text: I recommend you watching José’s talk introducing Elixir Nx

gmn7tjSNyAA.title: How to grow fresh air | Kamal Meattle
gmn7tjSNyAA.summary: Researcher Kamal Meattle describes how an arrangement of three common houseplants placed in specific spots can measurably clean the air in a home or office. It is a short TED talk based on his work in a plant-filled building.
gmn7tjSNyAA.why: HN commenters cite it in threads about indoor air quality, CO2 and houseplants as a cheap, low-tech approach.

quote.text: There is also a Ted talk about taking this to an extreme, which does seem to anecdotally work

Bmz67ErIRa4.title: Hackers (8/13) Movie CLIP - Hack the Gibson (1995) HD
Bmz67ErIRa4.summary: A short clip from the 1995 film Hackers in which the characters attempt to hack the Gibson supercomputer, shown with flashy stylized visuals of digital intrusion.
Bmz67ErIRa4.why: Used mostly as a punchline or example of cheesy, unrealistic Hollywood depictions of hacking and over-stylized tech UIs.

HRPDO63rI1E.title: "The Prisoner" Opening credits/sequence
HRPDO63rI1E.summary: The opening credit sequence of the 1960s British spy series The Prisoner, with Patrick McGoohan. It is a short intro to a cult TV show.
HRPDO63rI1E.why: HN commenters mostly reference it as shorthand for a reality that feels like a trap, often alongside The Truman Show, rather than recommending it.

IKVFZ28ybQs.title: Automaton 2000 Micro - Dodging Siege Tanks
IKVFZ28ybQs.summary: A StarCraft 2 custom-map demo where a bot controls 100 zerglings against 20 sieged tanks and dodges the splash damage, leaving 19 survivors. The code was written in Blizzard's World Editor.
IKVFZ28ybQs.why: Cited in StarCraft and AI threads as a vivid example of superhuman micro and of machine speed advantage over humans.

quote.text: Zerglings vs Siege Tanks when controlled by AI with perfect micro.

Yf1o0TQzry8.title: Ilya Sutskever (OpenAI Chief Scientist) — Why next-token prediction could surpass human intelligence
Yf1o0TQzry8.summary: Dwarkesh Patel interviews OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever on time to AGI, what comes after generative models, data limits, alignment, and competing with Google. The title centers on whether next-token prediction could surpass human intelligence.
